contract: Valid Rust str scalar patterns and inputs; supplementary scalars stay single matching units
Backslash punctuation, control letters, c ASCII control, octal, x hex, u hex and paired UTF16 escapes
Quoted text including an unterminated final quote; following quantifier applies to the last quoted scalar
d D s S w W with Java default ASCII membership and scalar complements
Lower Upper ASCII Alpha Digit Alnum Punct Graph Print Blank Cntrl XDigit Space
Scalar ranges, nested union, negation and intersection/subtraction with nonempty operands
Java-accepted leading/trailing or otherwise degenerate ampersand intersections are not approximated
First successful prefix with continuation backtracking, not longest-match alternation
? * + {n} {n,} {n,m}, quantities up to Java signed-int maximum
Question-mark suffix preserves Java exploration order
Plus suffix prevents retreat after successful repetition
Plain parentheses affect matching; this prefix API does not expose group capture values
(?:expression)
(?>expression) discards only its own pending alternatives
^ $ A z Z and G for a fresh lookingAt call; CRLF has no interior default line boundary
i d m s x, on/off and scoped forms; lexical flag restoration at group boundaries
u and U, including Unicode case folding and Unicode character classes
Java-accepted c flag and canonical-equivalence matching
Unicode scripts/blocks/categories/binary properties and Java Character properties
b B, including Java21 nonspacing-mark inheritance even without U
R X h H v V and b{g}
N{name}
Rust str cannot represent lone UTF16 surrogate values; no replacement-character substitution
Positive/negative lookahead and lookbehind
Numeric and named backreferences
Named capturing groups
No group retrieval or capture history is claimed by the core prefix API
Only fresh lookingAt over a remaining-input slice is exposed; no find/replace matcher state
String pattern and embedded flags, like the existing RegexTokenParser constructor
looking_at may return a zero-width match, including EOF
token_prefix rejects EOF/zero-width and inverted success; inverted failure advances one scalar
Pattern size/depth/operands/instructions/set work and input/VM-step/backtracking-state limits
Expr compiled matcher reuse, Classic token propagation, sticky resource errors, both UBNF hosts and pre-generation support diagnostics
Java adapter retains standard Pattern without the Rust VM resource guarantees; Java stack/time containment remains required
